description: How do we keep astronauts healthy when they're thousands of kilometres away from a hospital? We're building a health monitoring solution to help astronauts track their health and stay safe during space missions.
summary:
Thryon is an offline-first health companion for astronauts on long-duration missions such as a journey to Mars. Far from Earth, communication delays mean a doctor is not instantly available, and most crew are not medical experts.

Thryon learns each astronaut’s personal baseline and flags changes against their own normal, not universal thresholds. Its core feature, Symptom Check, lets crew describe how they feel in everyday words. It returns a clear outcome (Informational, Monitor, Contact medical or Urgent) plus numbered self-care steps for when no doctor is on board, with no diagnosis or medication advice.

A live five-hazards check maps each astronaut’s data to NASA’s hazards of human spaceflight. A Radiation Monitor keeps measured dose, live NASA and NOAA space-weather forecasts, and modelled estimates clearly separate. Mental wellness check-ins, voice input and role-based privacy complete it, and everything works without a connection to Earth.

A 30-day Mars transit simulation shows four astronauts facing critical problems and recovering with Thryon’s guidance. Thryon matters because self-sufficiency is essential for crew health on deep-space missions.
